# Ezekiel 34 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The LORD gave me this message:

**2** "Son of man, prophesy against the leaders of Israel. Prophesy and tell them: This is what the Sovereign LORD says — What trouble awaits you shepherds of Israel who only take care of yourselves! Shouldn't shepherds take care of the flock?

**3** You drink the milk, wear the wool, and butcher the best animals, but you don't feed the sheep.

**4** You have not taken care of the weak. You have not tended the sick or bound up the injured. You have not gone looking for those who wandered away or were lost. Instead, you have ruled them with harshness and cruelty.

**5** So my sheep have been scattered because there was no shepherd, and they became food for every wild animal.

**6** My flock wandered over every mountain and every high hill. They were scattered across the whole earth, and no one went looking for them.

**7** Therefore, you shepherds, listen to what the LORD says:

**8** As surely as I live, says the Sovereign LORD, you abandoned my flock and left them to be attacked by every wild animal. Because you were no true shepherds — you fed yourselves but let my sheep starve —

**9** therefore, you shepherds, listen to the LORD's message:

**10** This is what the Sovereign LORD says: I now consider these shepherds my enemies. I will hold them responsible for what has happened to my flock. I will fire them as shepherds so they can no longer exploit the flock. I will rescue my sheep from their mouths.

**11** For this is what the Sovereign LORD says: I myself will search for my sheep and look after them personally.

**12** Just as a shepherd goes looking for scattered sheep, I will find my sheep. I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered on that dark and cloudy day.

**13** I will bring them back from among the peoples and gather them from different countries. I will bring them home to their own land. I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, beside the streams and in every green meadow.

**14** I will give them good pastureland on the high hills of Israel. There they will lie down in pleasant places and feed in the lush pastures of the mountains.

**15** I myself will tend my sheep and give them a place to lie down in peace, says the Sovereign LORD.

**16** I will search for my lost ones who strayed away, and I will bring them safely home again. I will bandage the injured and strengthen the weak. But I will destroy those who are fat and powerful. I will feed them — yes — with justice!

**17** And as for you, my flock, this is what the Sovereign LORD says: I will judge between one sheep and another, separating the rams and goats from the rest.

**18** Isn't it enough that you eat the best grass? Must you also trample the rest? Isn't it enough that you drink clean water? Must you also muddy the rest with your feet?

**19** Why should my flock have to eat what you have trampled and drink what you have muddied?

**20** Therefore, this is what the Sovereign LORD says: I myself will judge between the fat sheep and the thin sheep.

**21** You shove the weak aside with your flanks and shoulders, and you gore them with your horns until you have driven them all away.

**22** So I will rescue my flock, and they will no longer be abused. I will judge between one animal and another.

**23** And I will set over them one shepherd, my servant David. He will feed them and be their shepherd.

**24** And I, the LORD, will be their God, and my servant David will be their prince. I, the LORD, have spoken!

**25** I will make a covenant of peace with my people. I will drive away the dangerous animals so they can live safely in even the wildest places and sleep without fear.

**26** I will bless my people and their homes around my holy hill. I will send showers of blessing in season.

**27** The orchards and fields will yield bumper crops, and everyone will live in safety. When I break the chains of their slavery and rescue them from those who exploited them, then they will know that I am the LORD.

**28** They will no longer be prey for other nations, and wild animals will no longer attack them. They will live in safety, and no one will threaten them.

**29** I will give them a land famous for its crops, and they will never again suffer from famine or be mocked by other nations.

**30** Then they will know that I, the LORD their God, am with them, and they will know that they — the people of Israel — are my people, says the Sovereign LORD.

**31** You are my flock, the sheep of my pasture. You are my people, and I am your God, says the Sovereign LORD.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **34:2-4**: This passage is a devastating critique of abusive leadership. The leaders were supposed to care for the people, but instead they exploited them. God takes this personally — these are His sheep.

- **34:15-16**: God steps in to do what the leaders refused to do. He searches for the lost, heals the wounded, strengthens the weak. This is what real leadership looks like — and only God does it perfectly.

- **34:23-31**: The promise of 'my servant David' as the one true shepherd points forward to the Messiah. The New Testament directly connects this passage to Jesus, who calls himself the Good Shepherd in John 10.

— PNEUMA
